analysis:
Examined configuration.md:485–949, including native kernel admission/rollback, model hashing, memory/media budgets, prompt and SSD caches, environment scrubbing, cluster configuration, precision agreements and qualification diagnostics. The complete range map places the visible substantive changes at docs/reference/configuration.md:923–949; the preceding controls are unchanged, so their differences from historical T-041 prose are not established PR regressions.

The changed cluster-runtime-facts documentation introduces release registration of helper/capability digests, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications, from which an accepting coordinator derives approvals (923–935). This connects release publication (A-005, A-011) with qualification and serving authorization (A-017, A-016; T-052, T-054). It still describes member-side comparison against installed files, build-owned canonical computation, and exclusion of model IDs whose artifacts are described only as another registered model (935–949). No supplied implementation establishes an authorization bypass, weaker encryption, disclosure or billing change, and documentation alone does not prove that release publication now confers independent qualification.

Integration must examine ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.release, the release payload builder, member approval checks and the platform acceptance/derivation contract: are grants and parity qualifications independently approved and revocable, or merely trusted because a release registration includes them? Determine whether cluster qualification is distinct from A-017's App Attest qualification and whether the canonical model needs a new boundary. The external coordinator implementation and release/approval enforcement are outside these units; this remaining trust-contract question is material, not evidence of a regression. The truncated patch also contains later changes not visible in these units, which are not cleared by this pass.
